panels.title: Unified router: live routing traffic, backend health, and failover

options.content:
Telemetry from the SCM-supervised router on `127.0.0.1:18101`, scraped under the `fak_router` job. **This board is built on the router's own `fak_router_*` families** - the counters that actually move when the router forwards to third-party upstreams (hive-ai, nebius, opencode-go, ...). The older `fak_gateway_*` proxy counters (requests, streaming requests, upstream token totals, net-win gauges) are **structurally zero in routing mode** and are deliberately not plotted here: reading them made a busy router look idle. **Unavailable means missing evidence**, not zero: an absent series means the router did not report it, not that traffic is idle.

Common stats: **RPS** (now), **RPM** (1-minute rate), per-backend request share, error rate, attempt latency p50/p95, time-to-first-byte p50/p95, terminal-outcome mix, and failover rate. **Volume tiles and the per-backend / per-status attempt panels are windowed to the selected time range** - totals use `increase($__range)` and live rates use `rate($__rate_interval)` - so changing the range changes them instead of showing lifetime totals since process start. Two more sections: **caching** (prefix-cache hit rate, TTFB by cache hit/miss, cache-reported turns, prompt/cached token throughput) and **token throughput** (input / output / cached tokens per second from `fak_router_token_usage`).

panels.title: Traffic: live rate, volume, and concurrency
Router scrape (1 = reachable)
panels.description: Prometheus reachability of the SCM-supervised router listener on :18101. 0 means the router is up but unreachable to the container, or down; it is the scrape witness, not readiness.

panels.title: Requests per second (RPS)
panels.description: **The headline RPS**: upstream attempts per second the router is currently making, summed across every backend. In routing mode this is the real request rate (one logical request can fan into several attempts across a fallback chain, so attempt-rate is a slight upper bound on request-rate). A flat 0 with *Router scrape* = 1 means genuine quiescence.

panels.title: Requests per minute (RPM)
panels.description: **RPM**: the same attempt counter averaged over a fixed 1-minute window, times 60. Use this for capacity/throughput reporting where per-second noise is not useful. It is a rate over a fixed window, not the per-second rate the RPS panel shows.

panels.title: Success rate
panels.description: Share of terminal requests that succeeded (`served` or `served_fallback`) over all terminal requests, windowed. **The headline health number**: 1.0 is all success, and a drop is a serving problem. Read the outcome panel below to see which loss band grew.

panels.title: Total requests
panels.description: Routed requests completed across every terminal outcome, **windowed to the selected time range** (`increase` over `$__range`), from `fak_router_requests_total`. This is the routing-mode request total (unlike the structurally-zero `fak_gateway_requests_total` proxy counter it replaces). Change the range to see the volume for that window, not a lifetime total. In-flight requests are not yet counted here; see *In flight now*.

panels.title: Routing attempts (all backends)
panels.description: Upstream attempts **in the selected time range** (`increase` over `$__range`), across every backend, status, and fallback hop. **This is the router's real demand signal in routing mode** - one logical request can fan into several attempts across a failover chain, so this is >= the request total. A rising value with *Total requests* flat is the routing path, not an outage.

panels.title: In flight now
panels.description: Routed requests currently in flight (admitted, not yet terminal) - the router's live concurrency. A sustained high value with a low RPS means upstreams are slow, not that traffic is high.

panels.title: Backends: live health
panels.description: One row per configured backend: live in-flight attempts, consecutive failures since last success, seconds since the backend last succeeded, attempts in the selected time range, and how many of those were fallback hops. A backend with consecutive_failures > 0 and a growing seconds_since_success is failing over rather than serving. Series join on the `backend` label. The two attempt columns are windowed (`increase` over `$__range`), not lifetime totals.

panels.title: Errors per second by backend
panels.description: Per-second rate of failed upstream attempts, split by backend, from `fak_router_attempt_failures_total`. This is the router's own view of backend errors and is populated in routing mode (the structurally-zero `fak_gateway_*` counters are not used here). See the failure-class panel below for *why* they failed.

panels.title: Upstream error rate
panels.description: Share of upstream attempts that failed, windowed - the attempt-level error rate (a request can retry the next backend after a failed attempt, so this is deliberately separate from the request-level *Success rate*). A rising value means backends are rejecting or timing out.

panels.title: Attempt duration p50 / p95 by backend
panels.description: End-to-end upstream attempt duration (including body relay) at the 50th and 95th percentile, per backend, from `fak_router_attempt_duration_seconds`. This covers the whole attempt, so it tracks streamed response length as well as upstream speed.

panels.title: Time to first byte p50 / p95 by backend
panels.description: Time to response headers (time-to-first-byte) per backend, from `fak_router_attempt_ttfb_seconds`. This is the responsiveness an operator feels before decode starts; a high p95 here is upstream latency, not the router's own overhead.

panels.title: Requests by terminal outcome (per second)
panels.description: Per-second terminal-outcome rate from `fak_router_requests_total`. The `served` band is healthy completions; `served_fallback` is a failover success; `truncated`, `incomplete`, and `upstream_rejected` are the loss bands; `all_backends_failed` is a hard outage. Read this with the failure classes below to see what the loss responses were.

panels.title: Failure classes (per second)
panels.description: Per-second failed-attempt rate by routing failure class (e.g. `UPSTREAM_TIMEOUT`, `UPSTREAM_UNAVAILABLE`, `PAYLOAD_REJECTED`, `CONTEXT_OVERFLOW`), from `fak_router_attempt_failures_total`. This is the *why* behind the errors-per-backend panel.

panels.title: Attempts by backend
panels.description: Routing attempts per second partitioned by upstream backend (`rate` over `$__rate_interval`). A backend holding a flat share is not being selected for new work; a rising fallback-heavy backend is absorbing failovers. Windowed, so it reflects the selected range rather than a cumulative total since process start.

panels.title: Attempts by status
panels.description: Routing attempts per second partitioned by the upstream result (`rate` over `$__rate_interval`). The legend is the HTTP status the backend returned, except `0`, relabelled `0 (transport error)` because it is NOT a count of zero: a `0` status means the attempt never got an HTTP response at all (dial failure, timeout, reset). `402` is a credit wall, `429` rate limiting, `5xx` a backend fault. An absent series is unavailable evidence, never a healthy zero.

panels.title: Failover rate
panels.description: Share of *attempts per second* that were fallback hops over all attempts per second. A sustained rise means the primary backend is failing over. This is windowed (unlike a raw cumulative ratio) so it reflects current behaviour, not history since process start.

panels.title: Journal degraded by reason (per second)
panels.description: Rate of attached requests whose write-behind journaling stopped while the live stream continued, by reason, from `fak_router_journal_degraded_total`. A non-zero `store_error` or `quota` band means the router is serving but its durable request log is falling behind - traffic is unaffected, durability is.

panels.title: Routing topology is configuration, not a time series

options.content:
The routing topology (which backends exist, their weights, and the fallback chain) is **configuration**, not a metric. Read it live from the router itself:

```
GET /v1/router/summary
```

That endpoint returns the currently effective router configuration the SCM-supervised process loaded. The panels above show what that configuration is *doing* (attempts, errors, latency, fallbacks); the endpoint shows what it *is*. A config change is a discrete event, and this board does not record config history.

panels.title: Admission pressure
panels.description: Backpressure before the queue: outstanding admitted requests against the admission bound, plus the high-water mark since process start. **High water never decreases** (restart-only reset) - it answers whether the admission queue ever saturated. Outstanding flat near the bound with zero rejects is headroom, not failure.

panels.title: Admission rejects / s
panels.description: Per-second rate of requests rejected at admission, from `fak_router_admission_rejected_total`. Non-zero means the router is shedding load before routing; read it with *Admission pressure* to see whether the bound was actually reached.

panels.title: Durable store utilization %
panels.description: Write-behind durable store bytes against quota. **Sampled, not live**: the gauges refresh on a sampling cadence, so read the second series (`sample age s`) to know how stale the sample is; finished-but-unGCed records linger in it.

panels.title: TTFT p95 by model
panels.description: Time to the first token-bearing frame at the 95th percentile, per backend and requested model, from `fak_router_time_to_first_token_seconds`. Streamed attempts only - buffered traffic produces no series, so absence here is missing evidence, not fast TTFT.

panels.title: TPOT p95 by model
panels.description: Time per output token at the 95th percentile, per backend and requested model, from `fak_router_time_per_output_token_seconds`. Needs upstream-reported usage and at least two output tokens; an absent series is missing evidence, not zero pace.

panels.title: Prefix-cache hit rate
panels.description: Share of provider-reported prompt tokens that were served from cache, windowed: `cached_prompt_tokens / cache_reported_prompt_tokens`. The denominator is the REPORTED total - a vendor that stops reporting usage silently changes the ratio's meaning, so read gaps as missing evidence, not zero hits.

panels.title: Balancer snapshot age (s)
panels.description: Seconds since the balancer last took a share snapshot, per backend. It grows between split decisions: a large age with stable shares is normal under low traffic; a growing age alongside drifting shares signals a broken selection strategy.

panels.title: Backpressure fill, balancer strategy, and router state
Admission fill %
panels.description: Fraction of the admission bound held right now (`outstanding / bound`): 1.0 means the gate is saturated this instant. The raw gauges live in *Admission pressure*; its high-water mark never decreases (restart-only reset) and answers whether the bound was ever reached since boot.

panels.title: Balancer share ratio by group / backend
panels.description: Share of each group's SPLIT balance decisions that chose each member - a choice share, NOT an attempt share (fail-open decisions are excluded from the denominator). Compare it with the group's declared weights (configuration, not a metric - see the topology note above): a share converging off its weight is a silently broken selection strategy. **Absence = unmeasured, not 0**: the family is emitted only once a group has >= 30 split decisions, so low-traffic groups publish nothing; it is recomputed from the counter at each scrape, so its level drops after a counter reset. Read gaps against *Balancer snapshot age*.

panels.title: Balancer fail-open rate / s
panels.description: Rate of balance decisions made WITHOUT a usable snapshot (fail-open path: `reason` one of `saturated`, `unmeasured`, `no_snapshot`, `no_eligible_member`). These credit no member - the balancer ran and returned declared order instead of choosing. A sustained non-zero rate means the selector is running blind on stale or absent signals; pair it with *Balancer snapshot age* and *Balancer share ratio by group / backend*.

panels.title: TTFB p95 by cache hit / miss
panels.description: 95th-percentile time-to-first-byte split by whether the attempt was a prefix-cache hit or miss (`fak_router_attempt_ttfb_by_cache_seconds`, `cache` label). A large gap between the miss and hit lines is the cache paying for itself; a hit line that climbs toward the miss line means the prefix cache is not actually saving prefill. Windowed over `$__rate_interval`.

panels.title: Cache-reported turns / s
panels.description: Rate of turns the upstream reports as cache-eligible, per backend (`fak_router_cache_reported_turns_total`). This is the turn view of the prefix-cache hit rate's denominator: a flat line with a rising hit rate means the cache is working on a stable workload; a falling line means fewer turns are being reported as cacheable. An absent series is missing evidence, not zero turns.

panels.title: Prompt / cached / reported token throughput
panels.description: Prompt-token throughput per backend, split into the prompt total, the cache-reported total, and the cached total (all `rate` over `$__rate_interval`). The cached line under the reported line is the prefix cache actually serving tokens; the gap between reported and prompt shows how much of the prompt the vendor did not report as cache-eligible. Read the cached line against *Prefix-cache hit rate* for the ratio view.

panels.title: Token usage by type (tokens / s)
panels.description: Tokens per second by token type - input, output, and cached - from the GenAI-convention `fak_router_token_usage` histogram (`_sum` rate over `$__rate_interval`). This is the router's live token throughput: the output line is the generation rate, the input line the prefill load, and the cached line the prefix-cache savings. An absent series is missing evidence, not idle generation.

panels.title: Router state verdict: read live, no metric yet (gap)

options.content:
The whole-router **state verdict** (`ok` / `degraded` / `down`) and its reasons - including every `dead_ladder:<model>` chain whose declared fallback ladder has collapsed to one live rung - answer "which model chains are unusable right now". As of this board's contract there is **no Prometheus metric for it**: neither the router's own `:18101/metrics` fold nor the Fak Ops exporter (`fak_ops_*`) publishes a verdict series, so this panel documents the gap instead of plotting a proxy.

Read it live:

```
GET /v1/router/state        # verdict + reasons[]
fak-sync router state       # CLI view of the same document
```

Do not infer the verdict from `fak_router_backend_consecutive_failures`: that gauge is ONE input (the backend health streak). The verdict also folds zero-live backends, funding walls, config drift, and dead-ladder reachability; ladders past the cap collapse into a single `dead_ladder:+<count>` reason.
